Posted February 1, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: I find Kubby’s arguments quite convincing.)

From The American Medical Marijuana Association

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:
February 1, 2001

Why Patients Are Demanding Recall Elections
by Steve Kubby, AMMA Director

Last month, AMMA Director Lynnette Shaw shocked local officials by collecting enough signatures to force the Marin County District Attorney into a special recall election. Total cost: $15,000.

Now compare the cost for Marin medical marijuana patients to force a recall of their anti-medical marijuana D.A., versus the cost to one patient for a jury trial. Even if a patient can find an attorney to work for free, the cost of witnesses and court costs will usually exceed $15,000.

In our own case, my wife and I raised and spent over $300,000 to defend ourselves for two years, in a case that proved to be baseless and without any credible evidence against us. Although our trial ended in a 11-1 vote for acquittal, nearly two months ago, Placer District Attorney, Bradford Fenocchio has still not decided whether or not to retry us. In fact, we will have to wait until March 2nd to learn if we face yet another expensive
and stressful trial.
See
Kubby Trial Ends. Jury Split Eleven to One for Acquittal on Marijuana Charges. Prosecution’s Arbitrary Limits on the Number of Plants Fails. Significance for the Rest of California.

Now, as our prosecutor told our jury, " Do the math. " Compare the cost of recall to a jury trial. Even if a recall would cost a total of $50,000 for signatures and election campaigning, that is still one sixth the cost of the jury trial we just went through. Do the math and you'll see that patients have no choice, but to use recall elections to defend themselves.

Besides, if district attorneys are just going to ignore jury decisions, what choice do patients have? It makes far more sense for patients to pool their money and mount a successful recall to attack the problem at its root.

Many have warned us that recalls are dangerous because they usually fail. Others complain that another district attorney would probably be elected who is as bad or worse. But are these arguments valid?

Most recall elections are attempted by amateurs and have little support from the community, so failure is built-in. In contrast, AMMA's recalls are backed by seasoned activists who understand how to organize political support within our local communities. Moreover, there is a financial liability to these raids and prosecutions of patients that is very alarming to local taxpayers groups.

Why not wait until the regular elections to challenge hostile district attorneys? One reason is that it is a lot easier to get media coverage in a recall election, since it is a separate election and everyone loves a good fight. Furthermore, patients are under attack now and cannot afford to wait until the next regular election.

Thus far, the AMMA Recall Committee, under the direction of Dr. Jay Cavanaugh, has obtained bids for as little as $.75 per signature plus $.50 managing fee per signature. If we look at the number of voters in the counties that have the worst violations of medical marijuana rights, they turn out to be small counties, most with even less voters that in Marin.

Here are the actual numbers:

COUNTY REGISTERED VOTERS

Calaveras 24,791

El Dorado 94,278

Marin 146,152

Placer 145,509

Shasta 86,924

Sonoma 248,181

As you can see, all but Sonoma are even smaller than Marin County, where we have already been successful. If district attorneys are going to continue their dopey war on medical marijuana patients, then patients have no choice but to force recall elections and throw these corrupt D.A.s out of office.

Clearly, it is cheaper, less stressful and far more effective to spend money on recalling district attorneys, than for sick people to be forced to defend themselves in expensive show trials.
